title: Washington Ethics Advisory Opinion 25-03
text:
Opinion 25-03
Question:
I am a .60 FTE District Court Judge and also have a private practice. In 2021, I presided over a jury trial for an Assault 4th Degree DV case. The defendant was found not guilty. I was hired in the summer of 2024 by the victim of that case to represent her in a child custody case being heard in superior court. She is the respondent in the family law case. Petitioner is the defendant in the in the Assault 4th Degree DV case. Do I have a conflict in this matter?
Answer:
Because the two cases are related, a part-time judge should not represent the victim from an assault case in a subsequent family law matter involving the same parties when the part-time judge presided over the assault case. "A part-time judge shall not act as a lawyer in a proceeding in which the judge has served as a judge or in any other proceeding related thereto." CJC Application II(B). A part-time judge is defined as,
a judge who serves on a continuing or periodic basis, but who is permitted by law to devote time to some other profession or occupation and whose compensation for that reason is less than a full-time judge. A person who serves part-time as a judge on a regular or periodic basis in excess of 11 cases or 11 dockets annually, counted cumulatively without regard to each jurisdiction in which that person serves as a judge, is a part-time judge.
CJC Terminology.
The two cases are related because they involve the same parties and the assault charge may be an issue in the pending custody matter. Being the judge in an assault case, then representing the alleged victim in a subsequent case involving the same parties could negatively impact public confidence in the independence, integrity, and impartiality of the judiciary. CJC Rule 1.2. Therefore, a part-time judge should not represent any party in a subsequent related matter where the judge previously presided over a case involving one of the parties. CJC Application II(B).
This opinion is limited to the application of the Code of Judicial Conduct to part-time judges. GR 10. Any questions about the application of the Rules of Professional Conduct to a part-time judge in their role as an attorney should be submitted to the Washington State Bar Association.
1 Procedures, unlike substantive law, "involve the operations of the 'courts by which substantive law, rights, and remedies are effectuated.'" Waples v. Yi , 169 Wn.2d 152, 161, 234 P.3d 187 (2010) ( quoting
Putman v. Wenatchee Valley Med. Ctr. , 166 Wn.2d 974, 984, 216 P.3d 374 (2009)).
2 In an unpublished, Division 3 of our Court of Appeals held that ex parte submission of applications for extension of judgments under RCW 6.17.020(3) was appropriate and do not violate due process because the "debtor's due process right to contest liability was protected before the judgment was entered, and the limited risk of an irregular extension is adequately protected by the debtor's right to bring a postextension challenge...meaning there will seldom be a need for anything more than an ex parte procedure." Jones
v. Jones , 14 Wn. App. 2d 1038 (2020), rev. denied, 197 Wn.2d 1012, 487 P.3d 521 (2021).
